findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge (or explicitly scope out) the reconciler's direct-write CREATE path (apply_inbound_records.py:215), which bypasses create_core and so will not receive the REBAR_DETECTED_BY env stamp — either state it is intentionally uncovered or add a stamp at that seam like creation_channel does.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py:215 `create_path = _write_event_file(tracker_dir, local_id, "CREATE", create_data)` — a direct CREATE write
apply_inbound_records.py:208 self-documents: 'this inbound Jira CREATE is written DIRECTLY (bypassing composer.create_core), so we stamp the channel here'
Grep for "CREATE" writes under src/rebar/_engine confirms this is the sole create_core-bypassing CREATE writer
Plan Scope lists only composer.py, _processors.py, ticket_state.schema.json, docs — the reconciler write path is not enumerated
findings.finding: The plan's coverage claim (env read at create_core reaches 'library, MCP, and CLI filers') omits the reconciler's Jira-inbound CREATE path, which writes the CREATE event directly and bypasses create_core, so detected_by would never be env-stamped on that ingress.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — 'src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:create_core (:73) ... so library, MCP, and CLI filers all get the stamp'
scenarios: A bug ticket ingested via the Jira reconciler with REBAR_DETECTED_BY set in the environment — the field is silently NOT stamped because the write bypasses create_core
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Approach/Scope noting the Jira-inbound reconciler writes CREATE directly (bypassing create_core) and is therefore intentionally out of scope for detected_by (inbound imports are not a detection channel); if coverage IS desired, mirror the creation_channel stamp added at apply_inbound_records.py:214.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the proposed `detected_by` compiled-state field with the pre-existing `detected_by:` TAG NAMESPACE (reads.py:370-372, cli-reference.md:290, test_has_tag_detected_by.py): either project the stamped value into the existing tag/query path, explicitly supersede the tag convention, or justify why a second same-named mechanism must coexist — and state how metrics/`--has-tag` queries see both.
evidence: reads.py:370-372: `if has_tag.startswith("detected_by:") and not ticket_type: ticket_type = "bug"` — an established `detected_by:<source>` tag namespace, bug-only, already exists
docs/cli-reference.md:290 + src/rebar/_cli/help/list.txt:9: `tags matching ^detected_by: auto-intersect with --type=bug` — documented production convention

ABSENCE: the plan never mentions the existing `detected_by:` tag namespace; it treats detected_by as a greenfield field, so the two mechanisms (tag vs. compiled-state field) would coexist un-reconciled — same concept, same name, two data paths and two query surfaces
findings.finding: An existing `detected_by:` TAG NAMESPACE already captures the 'which channel detected this bug' concept — with query support (auto-intersects with type=bug), CLI docs, and tests — yet the plan introduces a NEW, same-named parallel `detected_by` compiled-state field + env var + flag without reconciling with or superseding it, risking a split-brain of two overlapping mechanisms for one concept.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — the whole detected_by field mechanism
scenarios: A filer sets REBAR_DETECTED_BY=canary (new field) while another workflow tags `detected_by:canary` (existing namespace) — metrics/queries now must union two sources or silently miss one
An agent runs `rebar list --has-tag=detected_by:canary` and gets NONE of the env-stamped bugs because those carry the state FIELD, not the tag
findings.suggested_fix: Add a subsection acknowledging the existing `detected_by:` tag namespace and choosing one path: (a) have process_create ALSO emit a `detected_by:<value>` tag so the existing `--has-tag` query + bug-intersect rule keeps working (single query surface), or (b) explicitly deprecate the tag convention in favor of the new field and note the migration for already-tagged bugs. Either way, keep the field↔tag relationship explicit so trends aren't split.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address the existing `detected_by:` tag namespace (reads.py:370, cli-reference.md:290, test_has_tag_detected_by.py): either justify why a NEW `detected_by` compiled-state field + env var is warranted over extending/reusing the established queryable tag channel, or reconcile the two — and resolve the `detected_by` field vs `detected_by:` tag name collision.
evidence: Existing prior art: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:370-372 — `if has_tag.startswith("detected_by:") and not ticket_type: ticket_type = "bug"` (detected_by:* tags are bug-only, auto-intersect with --type=bug)

tests/interfaces/queries/test_has_tag_detected_by.py seeds channel via `rebar.tag(bug, "detected_by:tests")` and lists via `has_tag="detected_by:tests"` — i.e. detection-channel-on-bug is ALREADY a first-class, queryable capability
`rebar.tag` resolves as a real exported API in the installed env
The plan text (Context/Approach/Scope) never mentions the `detected_by:` tag mechanism; it only cites the `creation_channel`/source_* projection as prior art
Naming collision: proposed compiled-state field `detected_by` vs existing tag prefix `detected_by:` — same word, two mechanisms
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new `detected_by` compiled-state field + `REBAR_DETECTED_BY` env var for capturing a bug's detection channel, but an existing `detected_by:` TAG NAMESPACE already captures the same intent (which channel found a bug) and is bug-scoped and queryable — the plan neither acknowledges this prior art nor justifies a second parallel mechanism.
scenarios: A filer sets REBAR_DETECTED_BY=canary AND another sets a detected_by:canary tag — two divergent records of the same fact, and escape-channel metrics could be split across both
An agent reads docs, sees `--has-tag=detected_by:*` already works for bugs, and is confused about which mechanism to use / which the metrics lens reads
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art' note comparing the two: (a) if the tag channel is insufficient (e.g. tags are user-editable/mutable while genesis provenance must be immutable, mirroring creation_channel's immutability guard), state that as the justification and explain how the metrics lens will treat tags vs the new field; (b) otherwise, prefer stamping a `detected_by:<source>` tag at create_core and drop the parallel field. Either way, rename to avoid the literal `detected_by` collision if both are kept.

findings.finding: The plan targets AUTOMATED filers (canary/CI/review-bot) but locates the env-var read at the CLI command module ('src/rebar/_commands/create.py (or the create command module)') with CLI-flag precedence, whereas library (`_lib_writes.create_ticket`) and MCP (`_mcp_writes.create_ticket`) ingresses converge on `create_core` WITHOUT going through the CLI arg parser — so an env read placed only in `create_cli` would fail to stamp REBAR_DETECTED_BY for python/MCP-based automated filers.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Scope bullet to place the env-var read in `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:create_core` (the seam every ingress converges on), passing an explicit `detected_by` param down from `create_cli`/`create_ticket`/MCP so the CLI flag can override the env-derived default without excluding non-CLI filers.
